question: How well does the Moto G Plus (Gen 5) handle everyday apps according to owners?
answer: No summary claims passed the evidence check.

Another reviewer described excellent performance in common apps with no lag even when rapidly switching between several large apps. [9e0feabcb4d1_2]

chunks.text: When it does I simply restart(power off and power back on) and it's buttery smooth again. Android has definitely come a long way and I'm very impressed. It's very well optimized. I also appreciate Google AI and Google Now. Google Assistant is very nice. Intuitive, intelligent, and simple. Kills Apple's Siri for sure. I use Google AI everyday and it definitely makes life easier! Combines weather, news, travel, shopping, and other information all in one place; laid out well and works wonderfully! In my opinion, Google and Android have over taken Apple and iOS. Android is now very optimized and efficient and on par with iOS if not better! The bonus is being able to customize it! If you're on a budget or simply don't want to spend $700+ on a device but want your monies worth. You won't find a better option out there for <$300!

Good phone, happy owner. Great phone for the money. While the processor is not much faster than the Galaxy S5 it replaced, but with the 64gB of RAM, I no longer bog down with multiple programs running. In daily use, it is very responsive. I *love* the fingerprint reader, which I've set to "One button nav" - took a bit of getting used to, but it works great (when my timing is "on"!). There's still a few "features" of Android 7 that I'm getting used to, but those are not a reflection on the phone itself.

Great phone for the price. This phone does not have all the bells and whistles. That being said this is a great budget phone. Camera isn't the best and the speakers aren't the best (audio out of the headphone jack is great), but this phone does have a very decent processor to handle all of your app needs. I use instagram, snapchat(sucks on android in general) facebook, and pokemon go without issues.
Good phone. Cant handle too many open apps without stutter.. Battery life good. Phone good. Camera good. Con: Can't handle too many open apps without stutter.

I thought it would be a really difficult switch to transition to Android but it really wasn't tough at all and this phone has a lot of great features that aren't available on the iPhone, I especially love the chop motion that turns the light on. I use that everyday just about and I absolutely love it. not only that but the phone keeps a charge for days it's super fast and it basically has any app that I want. So I guess for anyone that's a casual phone user like me I really don't see why you would pay the money for an iPhone when this is on the market.

I don't play games on my phone so I can't say whether it's good for that, but Spotify, YouTube and various social media apps work very well. Amazon Ads are not very intrusive, and if you want you can have apps (like Weather Channel) that have persistent notifications and it keeps the ads from covering your whole screen, it essentially turns them into a notification. I can't wait to see Motorola's next G device, this one has made me a big fan.

What I found are, relative to the iPhone, are: it does not focus as accurately and often missed focusing on people in photos, the shutter lag is very long, it does not do well in lower light situations, it can't handle backlit scenes very well, photos were generally darker lacking detail in shadows, and takes a very long time to save panorama photos. I actually ended up carrying my iPhone with me to take photos and only used the Moto if I wanted to immediately send the photo to someone. So, if you are a photo oriented person - I would be careful with this phone.

No need to contact anyone at T-mobile, manually set APNs, etc. Some things I particularly appreciate: - clean, near-stock Android 7.0 Nougat, like a Nexus or Pixel, without having to mess with third-party ROMs - no bloat, no Touchwiz, EMUI or other clunky skins. I did install Nova Launcher to stop Google Now from taking over my "swipe-left" home screen. - excellent performance in common apps. I don't play 3D action games, and so can't address those. With 4GB, 8 cores, and internal flash memory that seems faster than average, there's no lag even when rapidly switching between several large apps. Heavy multi-taskers should definitely spring for the 4GB model, and budget permitting, I'd recommend the same to anyone hoping to keep their G5+ for more than a couple of years, just for future-proofing.

Also, though, if I have an app that is particularly memory intensive (say, a game, or a large PDF), then the app itself will be quite slow and non-responsive. I have had a few "Force Close" incidents as well that I attribute mostly to lack of memory. As an addendum, I also learned after-the-fact that the version with amazon ads is the only version of these phones that cannot be "jail broken" for installing custom android versions. This actually makes sense in retrospect, as I would likely be able to remove the ads feature if I did this. I thought I would include this, though, for anyone else that is interested in "rooting" their device. The inability to jail brake the device, though, has not contributed to my 2-star rating

It allows you to swipe left,right,etc... and access functions and features. It still have the Moto gestures that are features Google should have included from the beginning. The processor is fast enough for most people's everyday use, but it won't play high end graphic intensive games without shutter or lag. But then, if your getting a phone to play those, you probably are not going to get this phone anyways. So... great phone and great price.
